claim: The paper studies training-inference mismatch from numerical implementation differences and stale sampler checkpoints.
notes: Distinguish numerical TIM from policy staleness; both make sampler q differ from trainer p.

claim: Full sequence importance sampling requires behavior-policy support wherever the target policy has support.
notes: The paper's exact identity is sequence-level; practical token-level estimators target different surrogates.

claim: Importance ratios can have high variance and clipping or truncation changes the estimator.
notes: Do not treat PPO, GRPO and DAPO as identical clipping implementations.

claim: The score is the parameter gradient of token log probability and has zero expectation under its own policy.
notes: Score is a parameter-space vector, not scalar log probability.

claim: The off-policy expected gradient decomposes into E_q[A] E_q[s] plus Cov_q(A,s).
notes: The decomposition is conditional on a fixed prefix h.

claim: With q fixed, the sampler expected score is the negative gradient of KL(q||p).
notes: State the KL direction explicitly rather than using forward/reverse labels alone.

claim: Group centering does not make conditional expected advantage zero at every prefix.
locator: §4, Group centering does not remove drift
notes: Group centering can shrink drift but does not eliminate per-prefix drift.

claim: Score centering subtracts the sampler expected score and leaves reward-score covariance under q.
notes: This removes drift at a fixed prefix; it does not turn q into p.

claim: The top-k approximation uses sampler probabilities on the head and rescales trainer probabilities on the tail.
notes: Tail-shape assumption is approximate; original experiments use k=128 and report k=32 also matches tested settings.

claim: The score-centering loss uses stop-gradient coefficients in a scalar autograd objective.
notes: Actual trainers additionally need token masks, normalization, numerical guards and distributed implementation.

claim: The paper reports top-k 128 and 32 matching full score centering in its tested settings.
notes: Empirical result, not a universal approximation guarantee.

claim: Score centering is a drift/bias correction, not a general variance-reduction theorem.
notes: Do not claim deterministic score subtraction always reduces estimator variance.

claim: The remaining score-centered update measures covariance under sampler q rather than trainer p.
notes: It does not remove all off-policy bias or prefix distribution mismatch.

claim: Main experiments use Qwen3-0.6B Countdown and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base INTELLECT-2 math under deliberately severe mismatch.
notes: Authors describe severe mismatch on shorter sequences as a proxy for longer training under milder mismatch.

claim: Under INT8 sampler and INT4 KV cache, the paper reports SC around 30% training accuracy, TIS 12%, and other methods below 5%.
notes: Training accuracy under the stated severe quantization setting, not independent test accuracy.

claim: The official implementation provides JAX and PyTorch reference losses, top-k capture and TIS/MIS composition.
notes: Reference implementation and reproducibility code, not a universal production trainer.

claim: verl documents score centering with bypass REINFORCE and top-k log probabilities, with configuration restrictions.
notes: Current docs list restrictions including no sequence-level IS in this mode.

claim: NeMo-RL nightly documentation describes score centering as experimental and requiring supported rollout capture.
notes: Experimental status and supported layouts are version-dependent.

claim: Regularized Score Centering adds reverse KL(pi_theta||mu) to constrain learner-behavior policy separation.
notes: November 2026 follow-up preprint, not part of original SC.

claim: RSC motivates its regularizer because token advantages depend on behavior-policy continuations and may differ from learner-policy advantages.
notes: This clarifies continuation mismatch not removed by local score centering.

claim: A 2026 theory note distinguishes group-mean baseline from population score centering and analyzes sequence-level versus token-level IS.
notes: Treat as follow-up analysis, not a claim from the original paper.

claim: The Bernoulli interactive example verifies drift/signal decomposition and zero centered expected update under constant reward.
notes: One-parameter toy model, not an LLM benchmark or paper reproduction.
